chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Harith ibn Bahram, from Amr ibn Jumi', who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who comes to us seeking jurisprudence and the Quran and its interpretation, invite him; and the one who comes to us showing openly what Allah has veiled, turn him away.'

A man from the group said to him: 'May I be sacrificed for you! By Allah, I have been persisting upon a sin for a long time. I intend to turn away from it to something else, but I am not able to do so.'
He said to him: 'If you are truthful, then Allah loves you, and nothing prevents Him from transferring you from it to something else except that you fear Him.'

key_terms.عَوْرَةً: Awnah (that which should be covered/shown modestly)

ai.seo_question: Why does a person persist in sin despite wanting to repent?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contrasts the reception of the learned with the dismissal of those who ostentatiously display their sins, highlighting the spiritual danger of *al-Lamam* (persistence in sin). He explains that Allah’s delay in transferring a persistent sinner to a different state is not due to lack of power, but to preserve their *khawf* (awe/fear), which serves as the necessary restraint preventing them from falling deeper into transgression. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the dialectic between hope (*rajā'*) and fear (*khawf*) in maintaining spiritual equilibrium.

en.hubeali: Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Haris Bin Bahran, from Amro Bin Jumi’e who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who comes to us<sup>asws</sup> seeking the jurisprudence, and the Quran and its interpretation, so invite him; and the one who comes to us<sup>asws</sup> showing openly what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Veiled, so prevent him’.

So a man from the group said to him<sup>asws</sup>: ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I have been staying upon a sin since forever (since a long time). I intend to transfer away from it to other than it, but I am not able upon it’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘If you were truthful, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Loves you, and nothing is preventing you from transferring from it to other than it except you are fearing Him<sup>azwj</sup> (which is why you are intending as such)’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from al-Harith ibn Bahram from ‘Amr ibn Jumay’ who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Whoever comes to us seeking to learn Fiqh (laws of Shari’a) and the Holy Quran, allow him to come in. Whoever comes to us to make public what Allah has covered, you must move him away.’
A man from the people then said, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I have been involved in sin for a long time and I want to change to something else but I am not able to do so.’
The Imam said, ‘If you are true, Allah loves you. There is nothing to prevent Him from changing you to something else, it is only as such so that you can be fearing Him.’”
